newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weighs new diplomatic push on Aegean, Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weighs new diplomatic push on Aegean, Cyprus.

text.p: The United States told Greece Tuesday it was hoping to lead a new effort to resolve Greco- Turkish tensions over the Aegean Sea, and also wanted to be more active on Cyprus, the State Department said.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said Secretary of State Warren Christopher passed the message to Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos at a meeting in New York, where both are attending the U.N. General Assembly.

"Secretary Christopher said that he thought that it was important for the United States to help lead a new effort to resolve some of the Aegean problems between Greece and Turkey," Burns told reporters.

He said U.N. ambassador Madeleine Albright and Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs Peter Tarnoff would be "closely involved" in the effort, but said no dates were discussed for any mission or meeting.

Greece and Turkey have long been involved in disputes over ownership of certain Aegean islands as well as airspace and seabed rights. They nearly came into conflict early this year over a small and uninhabited islet.
That dispute prevented a mission that former U.S. assistant secretary of state Richard Holbrooke was to have made to the region in February to tackle the Cyprus problem.
Christopher told Pangalos that following Greek elections last Sunday, he hoped Washington could be more active over Cyprus, where a Greek and a Turkish Cypriot have been killed in recent incidents.

The Mediterranean island has been divided between its Greek and Turkish communities since a 1974 invasion by mainland Turkey in response to a Greek Cypriot military coup in Nicosia. Repeated U.N. mediation attempts have failed to reunify Cyprus.
Burns said that on both the Aegean and Cyprus, "no decisions have been made. The Secretary and the Minister did not go into detail ... It was a general discussion."

The spokesman said that Pangalos had welcomed a U.S. role and that Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller had agreed with Christopher at a meeting Monday that now would be a good time "to see what can be done" on both issues.
